header.running_head: The Marriages of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA)

blocks.text: then (remember that) Allaah certainly has knowledge of everything (and will take you to task for it).
Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ recited these verses to me before anyone else, making me the first person to have the honour of hearing them." [^1]
Rasulullaah ﷺ's Marriage to Hadhrat Safiyya bint Huyay bin Akhtab (RA)

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that when the prisoners captured after the Battle of Khaybar were mustered together, Hadhrat Dihya (RA) approached Rasulullaah ﷺ with a request. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" he said, "Give me a slave woman from the captives." "Go and take one," Rasulullaah ﷺ said. Hadhrat Dihya (RA) proceeded to take Safiyya bint Huyay. Someone then came to Rasulullaah ﷺ saying, "O Nabi of Allaah ﷺ! You have given to Dihya Safiyya bint Huyay who is the leader of the Banu Qurayzah and Banu Nadheer tribes! She is suitable only for you." Rasulullaah ﷺ then sent for her and when he saw her, he instructed Hadhrat Dihya (RA) to take another woman. Rasulullaah ﷺ then set her free and married her. [^2]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that they marched to Khaybar and after conquering the fortress there, Rasulullaah ﷺ was informed about Safiyya bint Huyay bin Akhtab. She was an extremely beautiful lady whose husband had been killed while she was still a new bride. Rasulullaah ﷺ chose (to marry) her and (after leaving Khaybar) it was only when they reached the boundary of Sahbaa that she stopped menstruating. It was therefore only there that Rasulullaah ﷺ was able to consummate the marriage. Rasulullaah ﷺ then had some Hais [^3] prepared and served on a leather tablecloth. Hadhrat Anas (RA) was then instructed to invite whoever was in the area (to partake of the food). This was the Waleemah meal for Rasulullaah ﷺ's marriage to Hadhrat Safiyya bint Huyay (RA). Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports further that on the way back to Madinah, he saw Rasulullaah ﷺ use a shawl to make a screen for her behind him. He would then kneel beside his camel and place his knee upright for her to step on as she mounted the camel. [^4]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) states, "Rasulullaah ﷺ camped at a place between Khaybar and Madinah for three days. It was here that he consummated his marriage to Safiyya (RA), after which I invited the Muslims present there to a Waleemah meal that featured neither bread nor meat. All that it consisted of was Rasulullaah ﷺ's instruction to Bilaal (RA) to spread out a leather tablecloth. He then scattered some dates, cheese and butter onto it (which the people ate). Some of the Muslims asked, 'Is she one of the Ummahaatul Mu'mineen (wives of Rasulullaah ﷺ) or his slave woman?' Others replied, 'If Rasulullaah ﷺ veils
Ibn Abi Haatim, Muslim, Nasa'ee, Tirmidhi, Bukhaari and Ibn Jareer, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.4 Pg.146). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.8 Pg.104) has reported a similar narration.
